summary:
Bank research this week centered on the September FOMC's hawkish surprise: Goldman flagged a 16-2 dot-plot majority for at least one more 2026 hike and now expects a second 25bp hike in October, while BofA held its call for two more 25bp hikes in October and December. Goldman's broader desk output covered the market fallout — one of the worst 5-year real bond returns in a century, mega-cap valuations still below their 10-year average, and earnings as the main driver of 2025 returns — plus a diesel-vs-gasoline refining spread call and a stable-consumer survey. BofA also tracked rising commercial/industrial electricity demand and a 5.3% YoY jump in utility bill payments. No cross-source duplicate charts were found this cycle.
Per-bank counts: Goldman 9, BofA 3.
